title: Surface group character varieties
summary: The action of TeichmullerGeometry's outer automorphism group on conjugacy classes of homomorphisms; the punctured-surface mapping class group completed by the marked-point comparison, the pure group and the pure Birman sequence; the outer action Psi of Mod_{g,n} on pi_1; representation schemes of finitely generated groups; real reductive data, the real-form bridge and the real Kempf-Ness theorem; the six characterizations of reductive representations; and the character variety X(Gamma, G^R) of a finitely generated group, Hausdorff, locally compact and second countable, homeomorphic to minimal vectors modulo K, equal for complex groups to the complex points of Hom(Gamma,G)//G, with Out(Gamma) and Mod_{g,n} acting by homeomorphisms.

layers.title: Outer automorphisms and conjugacy classes of homomorphisms

targets.name: OuterAut.congr
targets.statement: Out(Γ) is TeichmullerGeometry §4.2's OuterAut Γ = MulAut Γ ⧸ range(MulAut.conj). The kernel of MulAut.conj : Γ →* MulAut Γ is Z(Γ), so Γ ⧸ Z(Γ) ≃* Inn(Γ). An isomorphism e : Γ ≃* Γ' induces Out(Γ) ≃* Out(Γ'), [φ] ↦ [e ∘ φ ∘ e⁻¹], by descending MulAut.congr e; functorial in e; an inner e = MulAut.conj g induces the identity of Out(Γ).

tests.name: inn_Q8
tests.statement: Z(Q₈) = {±1}, Inn(Q₈) ≅ Q₈/{±1} is the Klein four-group of order 4 (not 8); with |MulAut Q₈| = 24 the quotient has TeichmullerGeometry §4.2's value |Out(Q₈)| = 6.

tests.name: inn_Z_S3
tests.statement: Z(ℤ) = ℤ and Inn(ℤ) is trivial; Z(S₃) = 1 and Inn(S₃) ≅ S₃ has order 6.

tests.name: inner_transport_Q8
tests.statement: For e = MulAut.conj i on Q₈, MulAut.congr e is conjugation in MulAut Q₈ ≅ S₄ by a nontrivial element of V₄ = Inn(Q₈), nontrivial on S₄ (trivial centre) but trivial on Out(Q₈) ≅ S₄/V₄ ≅ S₃.

tests.name: outer_transport_Z2
tests.statement: For Γ = ℤ² and e = diag(1,−1), the induced automorphism of Out(ℤ²) = GL₂(ℤ) is conjugation by diag(1,−1), sending [[1,1],[0,1]] to [[1,−1],[0,1]].

targets.name: HomConj
targets.statement: Rep(Γ, H) := (Γ →* H) modulo the orbit relation of ConjAct H acting by postcomposition: ρ ∼ MulAut.conj h ∘ ρ.

api.name: HomConj.mk_eq_mk_iff
api.statement: [ρ] = [ρ'] iff ρ' = MulAut.conj h ∘ ρ for some h.

api.name: HomConj.mapTarget
api.statement: H →* H' induces Rep(Γ,H) → Rep(Γ,H'), functorially.

api.name: HomConj.mapSource
api.statement: Γ' →* Γ induces Rep(Γ,H) → Rep(Γ',H), contravariantly functorially.

api.name: HomConj.equivOfComm
api.statement: For commutative H the quotient map Hom(Γ,H) → Rep(Γ,H) is a bijection.

api.name: HomConj.intEquivConjClasses
api.statement: Rep(ℤ, H) ≃ ConjClasses H via [ρ] ↦ [ρ 1].

tests.name: rep_int_S3
tests.statement: Rep(ℤ, S₃) has 3 elements while Hom(ℤ, S₃) has 6.

tests.name: rep_trivial_target
tests.statement: Rep(Γ, 1) is a point for every Γ.

tests.name: rep_Z2_GL2
tests.statement: Rep(ℤ/2, GL₂(ℂ)) has 3 elements (eigenvalue multisets of involutions) while Hom(ℤ/2, GL₂(ℂ)) is infinite.

targets.name: HomConj.outAction
targets.statement: φ·ρ = ρ ∘ φ⁻¹ is a left action of MulAut Γ on Γ →* H commuting with H-conjugation; MulAut.conj γ · ρ = MulAut.conj (ρ γ)⁻¹ ∘ ρ; hence Out(Γ) acts on Rep(Γ,H) by [φ]·[ρ] = [ρ ∘ φ⁻¹], naturally in H. Inn(Γ) acts trivially on Γ →* H iff every homomorphism Γ → H has commutative image.

locator.where: lines 41–50, Definition 1.1.1 and the following paragraph

tests.name: left_action_witness
tests.statement: On ℤ² with ρ the first coordinate, φ = [[1,1],[0,1]], ψ = [[1,0],[1,1]]: (φψ)·ρ = (1,−1) = φ·(ψ·ρ) while ψ·(φ·ρ) = (2,−1).

tests.name: inner_free_nontrivial
tests.statement: For Γ = H = F₂ and ρ = id, MulAut.conj a · id = MulAut.conj a⁻¹ ≠ id, with the same class.

tests.name: abelian_target
tests.statement: For commutative H, Inn(Γ) acts trivially on Hom(Γ,H).

layers.title: Punctured surfaces, marked points and the pure mapping class group

targets.name: Homeomorph.isotopyClasses
targets.statement: Homeo₀(X) := {Φ.finalHomeomorph | Φ : TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy X} is a normal subgroup of X ≃ₜ X; Mod^±(X) := (X ≃ₜ X) ⧸ Homeo₀(X), differing from TeichmullerGeometry §0.0h's MappingClassGroupFull X by requiring the level-preserving total map of an isotopy to be a homeomorphism; the identity of X ≃ₜ X induces a surjection Mod^±(X) → MappingClassGroupFull X, an isomorphism for X compact, connected, Hausdorff and charted on a finite-dimensional real normed space, and for a closed surface Σ_g, composed with TeichmullerGeometry §0.0h's forgetful isomorphism, an identification with GeometricTopology Layer 1.7.2's Mod(F) for a smooth structure F on Σ_g; for X a topological manifold without boundary charted on a finite-dimensional real normed space, every homotopy through homeomorphisms from the identity is an ambient isotopy (invariance of domain); for locally compact Hausdorff X, with the topology induced by f ↦ (f, f⁻¹) into C(X,X)² (compact-open), X ≃ₜ X is a topological group and Homeo₀(X) is the identity path component.
hypotheses: X a topological space; locally compact Hausdorff for the path-component clause; compact, connected, Hausdorff and charted on a finite-dimensional real normed space for the isomorphism with MappingClassGroupFull X; a topological manifold without boundary charted on a finite-dimensional real normed space for the homotopy-to-ambient-isotopy clause

api.name: Homeomorph.isotopyClasses.normal
api.statement: Homeo₀(X) is a normal subgroup.

api.name: Homeomorph.isotopyClasses.mk_eq_mk_iff
api.statement: [f] = [g] iff f and g are TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.

api.name: Homeomorph.isotopyClasses.congr
api.statement: X ≃ₜ Y induces Mod^±(X) ≃* Mod^±(Y) by conjugation.

api.name: Homeomorph.isotopyClasses.of_compact
api.statement: For compact Hausdorff X every homotopy through homeomorphisms from the identity is an ambient isotopy.

api.name: Homeomorph.isotopyClasses.of_boundaryless_manifold
api.statement: For a topological manifold X without boundary charted on a finite-dimensional real normed space, every homotopy I × X → X through homeomorphisms from the identity is an ambient isotopy: extended by its end maps to ℝ × X its level-preserving total map is a continuous bijection of ℝ × X onto itself, open by invariance of domain (Continuous.isOpenEmbedding_of_injective). Hence MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.9's isotopies of Σ_g ∖ P (paths in §5.17's Homeo⁺ with the compact-open topology) are the ambient isotopies.

api.name: Homeomorph.isotopyClasses.mem_iff_joined
api.statement: For locally compact Hausdorff X, f ∈ Homeo₀(X) iff f is joined to 1 in the two-sided compact-open topology.

api.name: Homeomorph.isotopyClasses.toMappingClassGroupFull
api.statement: The identity of X ≃ₜ X induces a surjective homomorphism Mod^±(X) → MappingClassGroupFull X (TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.isotopic), bijective for compact connected Hausdorff X charted on a finite-dimensional real normed space (TauCeti.isotopic_iff_ambientIsotopic), in particular for closed surfaces read on the boundaryless model (TeichmullerGeometry §0.0e). Composed with TeichmullerGeometry §0.0h's forgetful isomorphism it identifies Mod^±(Σ_g) with GeometricTopology Layer 1.7.2's Mod(F) for a smooth structure F on Σ_g, the owner of the mapping class groups of compact surfaces.

tests.name: mod_real_line
tests.statement: Mod^±(ℝ) has two elements (monotonicity type is an isotopy invariant).

tests.name: mod_two_points
tests.statement: For the discrete two-point space Mod^± has two elements; for a point it is trivial.

tests.name: mod_circle
tests.statement: Mod^±(S¹) has two elements (degree is an isotopy invariant, rotations are isotopic to id).

targets.name: Homeomorph.extendPunctures
targets.statement: Restriction Homeo(Σ,P) → (Σ∖P) ≃ₜ (Σ∖P) is a group isomorphism; ambient isotopies of Σ∖P extend uniquely to ambient isotopies of Σ fixing P pointwise; Mod^±(Σ∖P) ≅ Homeo(Σ,P)/(isotopy rel P); for Σ = Σ_g oriented, Mod_{g,n} of MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.9, whose isotopies (paths in §5.17's Homeo⁺(Σ_{g,n})) are the ambient isotopies of Σ_{g,n} by 2.1, is the orientation-preserving subgroup and ≅ Homeo⁺(Σ_g,P)/(isotopy rel P).
hypotheses: each p ∈ P has a basis of compact neighbourhoods U with U ∖ {p} nonempty and connected

tests.name: two_punctured_sphere
tests.statement: Σ = S², P = {N,S}: (θ,s) ↦ (−θ,−s) on the cylinder extends to the rotation by π about an equatorial axis; Mod_{0,2} has two elements.

tests.name: circle_two_points
tests.statement: Σ = S¹, P two points: identity on one arc and reversal on the other has no continuous extension; punctured neighbourhoods are disconnected.

tests.name: empty_P
tests.statement: With P empty the isomorphism is the identity of Mod^±(Σ).

targets.name: MappingClass.permutation_surjective
targets.statement: σ : Mod_{g,n} → Sym(P) is a well-defined surjective homomorphism; PMod_{g,n} := ker σ has index n!.

tests.name: index_small_n
tests.statement: n = 0 and n = 1 give index 1.

tests.name: pants
tests.statement: (0,3): Mod ≅ S₃, PMod trivial, index 6 = 3!.

tests.name: annulus
tests.statement: (0,2): Mod has order 2, PMod trivial, index 2 = 2!.

targets.name: SurfaceGroup.homeomorphStandardModel
targets.statement: For every g ≥ 0, Σ_g (with its half-plane atlas of empty boundary) is homeomorphic to TeichmullerGeometry §0.0f's StandardSurface.model of StandardSurface.orientable g 0, the realization schemaRealization of its canonical word; hence Surface.IsOrientable Σ_g and Surface.genus Σ_g = g, so the genus of MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.4 and that of TeichmullerGeometry §0.0f agree on Σ_g. Route: classification_of_surfaces gives one standard model S; on the cell structure of the realization (one open disc, one edge per class of sides, one vertex per vertex class) the cellular boundary of the disc is the sum of the letters with their exponents, so H₂(S; ℤ) = 0 unless S = orientable g' 0, which has H₂ = ℤ and H₁ = ℤ^{2g'}; MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §§5.5–5.6 give H₂(Σ_g; ℤ) = ℤ[Σ_g] and H₁(Σ_g; ℤ) = ℤ^{2g}, so S = orientable g 0; StandardSurface.isSurface_model, invariance of orientability and StandardSurface.homeomorph_unique give the predicates.
hypotheses: Σ_g a closed connected oriented topological surface of genus g in the sense of MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.4 (MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.1 with empty boundary)

tests.name: torus_model
tests.statement: g = 1: the word a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹ has one vertex class and zero boundary map, H₂ = ℤ, H₁ = ℤ², so Surface.genus Σ_1 = 1.

tests.name: klein_bottle_excluded
tests.statement: nonorientable 2 0, word a a b b: boundary map 2a + 2b, H₂ = 0, H₁ = ℤ ⊕ ℤ/2; same Euler characteristic 0 and boundary count as the torus, so only H₂ (or the torsion of H₁) excludes it.

tests.name: genus_two_rank_only
tests.statement: Comparing only rank H₁ would accept nonorientable 5 0 (H₁ = ℤ⁴ ⊕ ℤ/2) as a model of Σ_2; its H₂ = 0 excludes it, and Surface.genus Σ_2 = 2.

tests.name: sphere_model
tests.statement: g = 0: word a a⁻¹, two vertex classes, d₁(a) = v₁ − v₀ ≠ 0, d₂ = 0, H₁ = 0, H₂ = ℤ, Surface.genus Σ_0 = 0; the projective plane a a has d₂ = 2, H₂ = 0, and is excluded.

targets.name: SurfaceGroup.fundamentalGroupEquiv
targets.statement: For g, n ≥ 0 and an enumeration of P there is S⁺(g,n) ≃* π₁(Σ_g ∖ P, x) carrying p_j to a based loop around the j-th puncture with the induced orientation; for n ≥ 1 the group is free of rank 2g + n − 1.

tests.name: pants_free
tests.statement: (0,3): free on p₁, p₂ with p₃ = (p₁p₂)⁻¹; three distinct peripheral classes.

tests.name: sphere_disc
tests.statement: (0,0) and (0,1): trivial groups; dropping peripheral generators would give ℤ² instead of F₂ for (1,1).

targets.name: MappingClass.pureBirman_exact
targets.statement: 1 → π₁(Σ_{g,n}, x) → PMod(Σ_g, P ∪ {x}) → PMod(Σ_g, P) → 1 is exact, with Push and the forgetful map.

tests.name: euler_zero
tests.statement: (1,0) and (0,2): injectivity fails (Push trivial on the torus; π₁ = ℤ for the annulus with PMod_{0,3} trivial).

targets.name: MappingClass.congrOfPair
targets.statement: An orientation-preserving homeomorphism of pairs e : (Σ_g,P) → (Σ'_g,P') induces Mod_{g,n} ≃* Mod'_{g,n}, [f] ↦ [efe⁻¹], intertwining permutation maps; isotopic e induce the same isomorphism and different e differ by an inner automorphism; any two such pairs are related by some e (Σ_g ∖ P and Σ'_g ∖ P' have the same type (g, 0, n), so MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.4 gives an orientation-preserving homeomorphism, extended over the punctures as in 2.2).

tests.name: identity_pair
tests.statement: e = id induces the identity.

tests.name: self_pair
tests.statement: e ∈ Homeo⁺(Σ_g,P) induces conjugation by [e]; for Mod_{0,3} ≅ S₃ and e a transposition, conjugation by a transposition.

tests.name: orientation_reversing
tests.statement: An orientation-reversing e on the torus induces conjugation by diag(1,−1) on SL₂(ℤ), an outer automorphism.

layers.title: The outer action of the mapping class group

targets.name: Homeomorph.fundamentalGroupAut
targets.statement: f_δ := (fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath δ).symm ∘ FundamentalGroup.map f x : π₁(X,x) ≃* π₁(X,x), sending [γ] to [δ ⬝ (f ∘ γ) ⬝ δ̄].

api.name: Homeomorph.fundamentalGroupAut_changePath
api.statement: f_{δ'} = MulAut.conj [δ ⬝ δ̄'] ∘ f_δ.

api.name: Homeomorph.fundamentalGroupAut_symm
api.statement: (f⁻¹)_{rev(f⁻¹ ∘ δ)} = (f_δ)⁻¹.

api.name: Homeomorph.fundamentalGroupAut_refl
api.statement: id_{const} = 1 and, for a loop σ, id_σ = MulAut.conj [σ]⁻¹.

tests.name: convention_witness
tests.statement: For f = id and δ a loop σ, f_δ = MulAut.conj [σ]⁻¹; the opposite reading of fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath gives MulAut.conj [σ].

tests.name: circle
tests.statement: On S¹ with x = 1, complex conjugation acts by −1 on π₁ ≅ ℤ; rotation by π with an arc acts by +1.

tests.name: no_path
tests.statement: Without a path, FundamentalGroup.map f x lands in π₁(X, f x), not π₁(X, x), when f x ≠ x.

targets.name: Homeomorph.fundamentalGroupAut_of_homotopy
targets.statement: If H : f ≃ g is a homotopy of homeomorphisms with track η from f(x) to g(x), then g_{δ ⬝ η} = f_δ; if f ∈ Homeo₀(X) with track η : x ⟶ f(x) then f_δ = MulAut.conj [η ⬝ δ̄].

tests.name: point_push
tests.statement: For the push along a loop α, f_{const} = MulAut.conj [α], MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.19's γ ↦ α * γ * α⁻¹.

tests.name: torus_translation
tests.statement: A translation isotopy of the torus induces the identity.

tests.name: hyperelliptic
tests.statement: The genus-two hyperelliptic involution acts by −1 on the abelianization, not inner, hence not isotopic to id.

targets.name: MappingClass.outerAction
targets.statement: Ψ_x : Mod^±(X) →* Out(π₁(X,x)), [f] ↦ [f_δ], well defined and a homomorphism; for σ : x ⟶ x' the induced Out(π₁(X,x)) ≃* Out(π₁(X,x')) is independent of σ and intertwines Ψ_x and Ψ_{x'}; for X = Σ_{g,n}, Ψ_x[f] on Mod_{g,n} is the outer class of f_* through which MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.9's action on finite coverings factors, (f⁻¹)_* being Ψ_x[f]⁻¹; on Mod(S*) the based map [f] ↦ f_const lifts Ψ_x, and MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.19's Push(α), acting by MulAut.conj [α], is f_const for its end map by 3.2.

api.name: MappingClass.outerAction_mk
api.statement: Ψ_x [f] = [f_δ] for every δ : x ⟶ f(x).

api.name: MappingClass.outerAction_basepoint
api.statement: Ψ_{x'} = Out(fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath σ) ∘ Ψ_x, independent of σ.

api.name: MappingClass.basedAction_push
api.statement: MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.19's formula Push(α) ↦ MulAut.conj [α] is the instance f_const of 3.2 for the end map of the push.

tests.name: circle
tests.statement: Ψ : Mod^±(S¹) → Out(ℤ) = ℤ/2 is an isomorphism.

tests.name: torus_shear
tests.statement: The shear (u,v) ↦ (u, u+v) maps to [[1,0],[1,1]] in GL₂(ℤ) (matrices on column vectors); its transpose is the image of (u,v) ↦ (u+v, v).

tests.name: interval
tests.statement: For X = [0,1], π₁ is trivial while the flip is a nontrivial class: Ψ is not injective.

targets.name: MappingClass.outerAction_closed
targets.statement: For Σ = Σ_g closed connected oriented of genus g ≥ 1 and x ∈ Σ, Ψ_x corresponds under 2.1's isomorphism Mod^±(Σ) ≃* MappingClassGroupFull Σ to TeichmullerGeometry §5.4's dehn_nielsen_baer, hence is an isomorphism Mod^±(Σ) ≃* Out(π₁(Σ,x)); for g = 0 it is the map from the group of order two (TeichmullerGeometry §5.4a) to the trivial group. For g ≥ 1, Out(π₁(Σ,x)) acts on H₂(π₁(Σ,x); ℤ) (groupHomology of the trivial module, inner automorphisms acting trivially), H₂(π₁(Σ,x); ℤ) ≅ H₂(Σ; ℤ) ≅ ℤ by asphericity, and Ψ_x maps Mod(Σ) onto the index-two subgroup acting trivially on it, which, transported along TeichmullerGeometry §4.2's ι, is the group TeichmullerGeometry §5.4 writes Out⁺(Π), described here by the action on H₂; for g = 0 Out(π₁) and the image of Mod(Σ) are trivial. Sign step: f_*[Σ] = ε[Σ] and î(f_* u, f_* v) = ε î(u, v); invariance of î (MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.5) and its perfectness on H₁(Σ; ℤ) ≅ ℤ^{2g} ≠ 0 (MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §§5.5–5.6) give ε = 1 for orientation-preserving f; the reflection r induced by z ↦ e^{2πi/g} z̄ on the realization of the canonical word (2.4a) has ε = −1. The hypotheses Surface.IsOrientable Σ and 1 ≤ Surface.genus Σ of dehn_nielsen_baer come from 2.4a.
hypotheses: Σ = Σ_g a closed connected oriented surface
g ≥ 1 for the isomorphism and the H₂ clause

tests.name: torus
tests.statement: Mod^±(T²) ≅ GL₂(ℤ) via H₁, inverse to TeichmullerGeometry §5.4a's mcg_torus_full; A acts on H₂(ℤ²;ℤ) = Λ²ℤ² by det A, so Mod(T²) maps onto SL₂(ℤ), index two; î(Au, Av) = det(A) î(u, v): the shear has ε = 1, diag(1,−1) has ε = −1.

tests.name: sphere
tests.statement: Out(1) is trivial while Mod^±(S²) has two elements: Ψ_x is an isomorphism for g ≥ 1 and not injective for g = 0; H₂(π₁(S²);ℤ) = 0 ≠ ℤ = H₂(S²;ℤ) and î = 0, so the H₂ clause needs g ≥ 1.

tests.name: genus_two
tests.statement: The hyperelliptic class maps to the outer class acting by −1 on the abelianization.

targets.name: MappingClass.actionHomConj
targets.statement: For every group H, the action of Mod^±_{g,n} on Rep(π₁(Σ_{g,n},x), H) is defined as Ψ_x followed by 1.3, [f]·[ρ] = [ρ ∘ Ψ_x[f]⁻¹]; for H = Sym(d), on transitive classes and on Mod_{g,n}, it is MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.9's action [p] ↦ [f ∘ p] on isomorphism classes of connected d-fold coverings under the monodromy correspondence (TauCeti.ConnectedCoveringSpace.monodromyEquivalence); it is compatible with basepoint change and H →* H'; orbits are finite under a finite-index subgroup (e.g. PMod_{g,n}) iff under Mod^±_{g,n}. Non-descent: for 2g − 2 + n > 0 and S = Σ_{g,n} marked at x, the based action [f]·ρ = ρ ∘ (f_const)⁻¹ of Mod(S*) on Hom(π₁(S,x), H) makes Hom(π₁(S,x), H) → Rep(π₁(S,x), H) equivariant for Mod(S*) acting on Rep through Forget, and it factors through Forget iff every homomorphism π₁(S,x) → H has commutative image (ker Forget = Push(π₁(S,x)), Push(α) acting by ρ ↦ MulAut.conj (ρ[α])⁻¹ ∘ ρ by 1.3 and MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.19).

locator.where: lines 41–50 (Definition 1.1.1 and the remark that Mod_{g,n} does not naturally act on the representation variety); lines 473–475 (PMod_{g,n} of index n!)

tests.name: finite_image
tests.statement: Classes with finite image have finite orbit.

tests.name: unipotent_genus_two
tests.statement: ρ(γ) = [[1,f(γ)],[0,1]] with f = a₁* on Σ₂ has infinite orbit (lines in H¹(Σ₂;ℂ) moved by Sp₄(ℤ)).

tests.name: abelian_target
tests.statement: For commutative H the action is through H₁, and the based action of Mod(S*) factors through Forget.

tests.name: coverings_comparison
tests.statement: On the torus, for the shear f (Ψ[f] = M = [[1,0],[1,1]]) and the triple cover with monodromy ρ(u,v) = v mod 3, f∘p has subgroup M(ker ρ) = {b ≡ a mod 3} = ker(ρ ∘ M⁻¹), as the definition [ρ ∘ Ψ[f]⁻¹] and MordellLawrenceVenkatesh §5.9's [p] ↦ [f ∘ p] both give, which fixes the direction of the definition; the right action ρ ∘ M gives {b ≡ −a mod 3}.

tests.name: push_moves_surjection
tests.statement: (g,n) = (0,3), π₁ = F₂ = ⟨a,b⟩, H = S₃, ρ(a) = (1 2), ρ(b) = (2 3): Push(a)·ρ sends b to (1 2)(2 3)(1 2) = (1 3) ≠ (2 3), so a class in ker Forget moves ρ.

tests.name: set_lift_exists
tests.statement: As an action on sets the action on Rep always lifts to Hom (fibres over one orbit are pairwise in bijection through ρ ↦ ρ ∘ φ⁻¹); for (0,3), H = S₃ it lifts the action on the 11 classes of Rep(F₂,S₃) to the 36 points of Hom(F₂,S₃), so 'no lift exists' is false and the theorem concerns the based action.

targets.name: RepresentationScheme
targets.statement: For an affine group scheme G over a commutative ring k (Hopf algebra A) and Γ with finite generating family s : S → Γ, the functor R ↦ Hom(Γ, G(R)) is represented by A^{⊗S} modulo the ideal generated by w*(a) − ε(a) for a ∈ A and w ∈ ker(FreeGroup S → Γ); independent of s up to unique isomorphism; finite type if A is; functorial in Γ and G; compatible with base change; G acts by conjugation.
hypotheses: G an affine group scheme over k

api.name: RepresentationScheme.pointsEquiv
api.statement: Hom(Γ,G)(R) ≃ (Γ →* G(R)), natural in R.

api.name: RepresentationScheme.evalGenerators
api.statement: Evaluation on s is a conjugation-equivariant closed immersion into G^S, an isomorphism for Γ = FreeGroup S.

api.name: RepresentationScheme.mapSurjective
api.statement: A surjection Γ' ↠ Γ induces a closed immersion Hom(Γ,G) → Hom(Γ',G).

api.name: RepresentationScheme.linearEmbedding
api.statement: For G ⊆ GL_N closed, ρ ↦ (ρ(s_i), ρ(s_i)⁻¹) is a closed equivariant immersion into (M_N × M_N)^S.

api.name: RepresentationScheme.baseChange
api.statement: Hom(Γ,G)_{k'} ≅ Hom(Γ, G_{k'}).

tests.name: free_and_cyclic
tests.statement: Hom(ℤ,G) = G, Hom(F_m,G) = G^m, Hom(1,G) = Spec k.

tests.name: mu2_char2
tests.statement: Hom(ℤ/2, 𝔾_m) over 𝔽₂ is Spec 𝔽₂[t]/((t−1)²), nonreduced; a points-only definition loses the nilpotent.

tests.name: commuting
tests.statement: Hom(ℤ², GL_n) has points the commuting pairs; omitting the relator gives GL_n × GL_n.

targets.name: RepresentationScheme.topology
targets.statement: Over ℂ the point topology on Hom(Γ,G(ℂ)) equals the classical topology and the pointwise topology; Hom(Γ,G(ℂ)) is closed in G(ℂ)^S, Hausdorff, locally compact. For a real reductive datum, Hom(Γ,𝐆(ℝ)) is the fixed set of complex conjugation on Hom(Γ,𝐆)(ℂ), Hom(Γ,G^ℝ) is open and closed in it, and G^ℝ acts continuously.

tests.name: GL1
tests.statement: Hom(ℤ, GL₁(ℝ)) = ℝ^× (two components); Hom(ℤ, GL₁(ℝ)⁰) = ℝ_{>0}.

tests.name: SO2
tests.statement: Hom(ℤ/2, SO(2)) = {±1} discrete; Hom(ℤ, SO(2)) is a circle.

tests.name: free_product_topology
tests.statement: Hom(F₂, G(ℂ)) has the product topology of G(ℂ)².

targets.name: RepresentationScheme.surfaceGroupEquiv
targets.statement: Hom(π₁(Σ_g,x), G) ≅ {(A_i,B_i) ∈ G^{2g} : ∏[A_i,B_i] = 1} and, for n ≥ 1, Hom(π₁(Σ_{g,n},x), G) ≅ G^{2g+n−1}, equivariantly for conjugation, with peripheral evaluations from the relator.

tests.name: torus
tests.statement: g = 1, n = 0: the commuting variety; 𝔾_m² for GL₁.

tests.name: pants
tests.statement: (0,3): G² with ρ(p₃) = (ρ(p₁)ρ(p₂))⁻¹.

tests.name: sphere
tests.statement: (0,0): a point; (1,1): G², not the commuting variety.

layers.title: Real reductive groups and minimal vectors

targets.name: RealReductiveDatum
targets.statement: A real reductive datum (𝐆, G^ℝ): 𝐆 connected reductive over ℝ and G^ℝ ⊆ 𝐆(ℝ) an open subgroup; G = 𝐆_ℂ, 𝔤^ℝ = Lie(𝐆), 𝔤 = 𝔤^ℝ ⊗ ℂ, Ad the adjoint representation; complex groups as Res_{ℂ/ℝ} H.

api.name: RealReductiveDatum.finiteIndex
api.statement: G^ℝ contains 𝐆(ℝ)⁰ and has finite index in 𝐆(ℝ).

api.name: RealReductiveDatum.ofComplex
api.statement: Res_{ℂ/ℝ} H with G^ℝ = H(ℂ) and 𝔤^ℝ = Lie(H) as a real Lie algebra.

api.name: RealReductiveDatum.Hom
api.statement: Morphisms of ℝ-groups mapping G^ℝ into G'^ℝ.

tests.name: SOpq_PSL2
tests.statement: SO(p,q)(ℝ) has two components for p,q ≥ 1; PSL₂(ℝ) = PGL₂(ℝ)⁰ is a datum.

tests.name: complex_GLn
tests.statement: Res_{ℂ/ℝ}GL_n: G^ℝ = GL_n(ℂ), dim_ℝ 𝔤^ℝ = 2n².

tests.name: excluded
tests.statement: The universal cover of SL₂(ℝ) and 𝔾_a(ℝ) = ℝ are not data.

targets.name: RealReductiveDatum.ofAntiholomorphicInvolution
targets.statement: For H connected reductive over ℂ and τ an antiholomorphic involution of H(ℂ), there is a connected reductive ℝ-group 𝐆_τ with (𝐆_τ)_ℂ ≅ H under which complex conjugation is τ, unique up to unique isomorphism; H(ℂ)^τ = 𝐆_τ(ℝ); conversely conjugations of ℝ-structures are antiholomorphic involutions; a holomorphic Cartan involution σ for τ restricts to an algebraic Cartan involution of 𝐆_τ with maximal compact fixed group.
hypotheses: τ an antiholomorphic involution of the complex Lie group H(ℂ)
prerequisites: roadmap:LieGroups Layer 7, Real forms and global descent
roadmap:LieGroups Layer 7, Compact-real-form pairs and algebraic morphisms

tests.name: GLn_forms
tests.statement: τ(g) = ḡ gives GL_n(ℝ); τ(g) = (ḡᵀ)⁻¹ gives U(n).

tests.name: quaternions
tests.statement: On GL₂, τ(g) = J ḡ J⁻¹ with J = [[0,−1],[1,0]] has fixed points [[a,−b̄],[b,ā]], the group ℍ^×.

tests.name: holomorphic_involution
tests.statement: g ↦ (gᵀ)⁻¹ is holomorphic with complex fixed group O_n(ℂ): not a real form.

targets.name: RealReductiveDatum.cartanRealization
targets.statement: There is a closed embedding 𝐆 ⊆ GL_N over ℝ with G^ℝ transpose-stable; G^ℝ = K exp(𝔭) and G(ℂ) = U exp(i𝔲) uniquely, with U and i𝔲 stable under conjugation and i𝔲 ∩ 𝔤^ℝ = 𝔭; the conjugation action on (M_N × M_N)^S with the trace inner product makes G^ℝ (over ℝ) and G(ℂ) (over ℂ) real reductive linear groups in the sense of BohmLafuente2021 (1).

tests.name: SL2
tests.statement: SL₂(ℝ): K = SO(2), 𝔭 traceless symmetric; minimal vectors of M₂(ℝ) are the normal matrices.

tests.name: GL1_scaling
tests.statement: GL₁(ℝ) on ℝ by scaling: only 0 minimizes the norm on its orbit.

tests.name: non_stable_embedding
tests.statement: SL₂(ℝ) conjugated by [[1,1],[0,1]] is not transpose-stable and the norm is not K-invariant.

targets.name: RealReductiveLinear.kempfNess
targets.statement: For G ⊆ GL(V) closed with G = K exp(𝔭): (i) M = {v : ⟨Av,v⟩ = 0 ∀A ∈ 𝔭} is a closed cone equal to the norm minimizers of each orbit; (ii) Gv closed iff Gv ∩ M ≠ ∅, then Gv ∩ M = Kw; (iii) a non-closed orbit has α ∈ 𝔭 with lim exp(tα)v outside Gv; (iv) each orbit closure contains exactly one closed orbit, containing the norm minimizers of the closure; (v) G = KTK for T = exp(𝔱), 𝔱 ⊆ 𝔭 maximal abelian, and disjoint closed T-invariant sets are separated by continuous T-invariant functions.
hypotheses: V a finite-dimensional real inner product space
G = K exp(𝔭), K = G ∩ O(V), 𝔭 = 𝔤 ∩ Sym(V)

locator.where: Theorem 1.1 (lines 77–88); Lemma 5.1; Corollary 5.5; Lemma 6.3; Corollary 6.4; Lemma 6.5; Corollary A.2

tests.name: hyperbolic
tests.statement: ℝ_{>0} on ℝ² with weights (1,−1): M = {|x| = |y|}; hyperbola branches and 0 are the closed orbits.

tests.name: SLn_conjugation
tests.statement: SL_n(ℝ) on M_n(ℝ): closed iff diagonalizable over ℂ; [[1,1],[0,1]] has the identity's orbit in its closure.

tests.name: scaling
tests.statement: ℝ_{>0} on ℝ by scaling: M = {0}; nonzero orbits are not closed; compact G: M = V.

targets.name: IsReductiveRep
targets.statement: ρ : Γ → G^ℝ is reductive when Ad ∘ ρ : Γ → GL(𝔤^ℝ) is a semisimple real representation (Representation.IsSemisimpleRepresentation); Hom^red(Γ, G^ℝ).

api.name: IsReductiveRep.iff_range
api.statement: Reductivity depends only on the subgroup ρ(Γ).

api.name: IsReductiveRep.conj
api.statement: Hom^red is stable under G^ℝ-conjugation.

api.name: IsReductiveRep.comp_surjective
api.statement: Hom^red is stable under precomposition with surjections Γ' ↠ Γ and automorphisms of Γ.

tests.name: trivial_rep
tests.statement: The trivial representation is reductive.

tests.name: unipotent
tests.statement: ρ(1) = [[1,1],[0,1]] in SL₂(ℝ) is not reductive: Ad ∘ ρ is a nontrivial unipotent.

tests.name: diagonal
tests.statement: ρ(1) = diag(2,3) in GL₂(ℝ): Ad ∘ ρ has eigenvalues 1,1,2/3,3/2 with a basis of matrix units; reductive.

targets.name: IsSemisimpleRepresentation.baseChange_iff
targets.statement: For k'/k and a finite-dimensional representation V of a monoid over k: V ⊗ k' semisimple ⇒ V semisimple; the converse for perfect k. Hence Ad ∘ ρ semisimple on 𝔤^ℝ iff on 𝔤; and for 𝐆 = Res_{ℂ/ℝ} H, Ad ∘ ρ on Lie(H) regarded over ℝ is semisimple iff the complex representation Lie(H) is, via W_ℝ ⊗_ℝ ℂ ≅ W ⊕ W̄.

tests.name: rotation
tests.statement: The rotation of order four on ℝ² is irreducible over ℝ and a sum of two characters over ℂ.

tests.name: unipotent
tests.statement: [[1,1],[0,1]] on ℝ² is semisimple neither over ℝ nor over ℂ.

tests.name: imperfect
tests.statement: Over k = 𝔽_p(s), k' = k(s^{1/p}) the converse fails (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §1.7's example).

tests.name: weil_restriction
tests.statement: For H = GL₂, Γ = ℤ: ρ(1) = [[1,1],[0,1]] gives a nontrivial unipotent Ad, semisimple on neither 𝔤𝔩₂(ℂ) nor ℝ⁸; ρ(1) = diag(2,3) is semisimple on both.

targets.name: adjoint_isSemisimple_iff_reductive
targets.statement: For G connected reductive over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and Z ≤ G closed, Ad|_Z on 𝔤 is semisimple iff Z⁰ is reductive.

tests.name: torus
tests.statement: A torus: reductive, 𝔤 splits into weight spaces.

tests.name: unipotent
tests.statement: The upper unipotent subgroup of SL₂: Ad not semisimple, not reductive.

tests.name: normalizer
tests.statement: N(T) in SL₂: disconnected with reductive identity component and semisimple 𝔤.

targets.name: isGCompletelyReducible_iff_reductive
targets.statement: For G as in 6.3 and Z a closed subgroup topologically generated by finitely many elements z₁,…,z_m, Z is G-completely reducible iff Z⁰ is reductive; the implication G-cr ⇒ Z⁰ reductive holds for every closed Z (gap gcr-reductive-identity-component).
hypotheses: Z a closed subgroup topologically generated by finitely many elements (for the reverse implication)

tests.name: irreducible_finite
tests.statement: The binary dihedral subgroup of SL₂ is in no proper parabolic, hence completely reducible and reductive.

tests.name: borel
tests.statement: The Borel of SL₂ is not completely reducible and has centralizer the centre: finite centralizer modulo centre does not imply reductive.

tests.name: GLV
tests.statement: For G = GL(V), complete reducibility is semisimplicity of V.

tests.name: normalizer_torus
tests.statement: Z = N(T) in SL₂(ℂ) is topologically generated by diag(2,1/2) and [[0,−1],[1,0]]; Z⁰ = T reductive, Z fixes no line, so Z is SL₂-completely reducible although disconnected.

targets.name: closedOrbit_iff_isGCompletelyReducible
targets.statement: For Γ finitely generated, G connected reductive over ℂ and ρ ∈ Hom(Γ,G(ℂ)): Zariski closure of ρ(Γ) G-completely reducible ⇔ G-orbit Zariski closed in Hom(Γ,G) ⇔ G(ℂ)-orbit classically closed.

tests.name: GLn_conjugacy
tests.statement: Γ = ℤ: the orbit of g is closed iff g is semisimple; [[1,1],[0,1]] has 1 in its classical closure.

tests.name: torus_valued
tests.statement: Torus-valued representations have closed orbits.

tests.name: borel_dense
tests.statement: ρ(a) = diag(2,1/2), ρ(b) = [[1,1],[0,1]]: conjugation by diag(t,t⁻¹), t → 0, tends to (diag(2,1/2), 1) outside the orbit.

targets.name: realOrbit_closed_iff_complexOrbit_closed
targets.statement: For a real reductive datum and ρ ∈ Hom(Γ,G^ℝ), Γ finitely generated: G^ℝρ closed in Hom(Γ,G^ℝ) ⇔ G(ℂ)ρ closed in Hom(Γ,G(ℂ)).

tests.name: rotation_unipotent
tests.statement: The rotation [[0,−1],[1,0]] in SL₂(ℝ) has closed real and complex orbits; [[1,1],[0,1]] has neither.

tests.name: abelian
tests.statement: ℝ^× acting trivially on Hom(ℤ,ℝ^×): all orbits are points.

tests.name: hyperbolic_element
tests.statement: diag(2,1/2) ∈ SL₂(ℝ) has closed orbit though not in K: compactness is not the criterion.

targets.name: isReductiveRep_tfae
targets.statement: For a real reductive datum, Γ finitely generated and ρ : Γ → G^ℝ, TFAE: (a) reductive; (b) Ad ∘ ρ semisimple on 𝔤; (c) Zariski closure Z has reductive Z⁰; (d) Z G-completely reducible; (e) G-orbit Zariski closed in Hom(Γ,G); (f) G^ℝ-orbit closed in Hom(Γ,G^ℝ). Compact image, Zariski-dense in reductive, and G-irreducible representations are reductive; for reductive ρ, G-irreducible ⇔ centralizer in G finite modulo the centre; for GL_r(ℝ), GL_r(ℂ): reductive ⇔ ℂ^r semisimple.

tests.name: unipotent_surface
tests.statement: ρ(a₁) = [[1,1],[0,1]], other generators trivial, on π₁(Σ₂) into SL₂(ℝ): all six conditions fail.

tests.name: borel_centralizer
tests.statement: The Borel-dense representation has centralizer the centre and is not reductive.

tests.name: compact
tests.statement: For SO(n) every representation is reductive and every orbit closed.

targets.name: CharacterVariety
targets.statement: For finitely generated Γ: 𝒳(Γ, G^ℝ) := Hom^red(Γ,G^ℝ)/G^ℝ with the quotient topology; (M ∩ Hom(Γ,G^ℝ))/K ≅ 𝒳(Γ,G^ℝ); 𝒳 is Hausdorff, locally compact and second countable; every orbit closure contains exactly one closed orbit.

api.name: CharacterVariety.mk_isOpenMap
api.statement: The quotient map from Hom^red is continuous, open and invariant.

api.name: CharacterVariety.lift
api.statement: Continuous G^ℝ-invariant maps from Hom^red factor uniquely through 𝒳.

api.name: CharacterVariety.minimalVectorsHomeomorph
api.statement: (M ∩ Hom)/K ≃ₜ 𝒳, independent of the realization up to homeomorphism.

api.name: CharacterVariety.t2Space
api.statement: 𝒳 is Hausdorff, locally compact and second countable.

api.name: CharacterVariety.closedOrbit
api.statement: Every orbit closure contains exactly one closed orbit, of minimal norm.

tests.name: compact
tests.statement: Compact G^ℝ: 𝒳 = Hom/G^ℝ, compact Hausdorff; agrees with HamiltonianReduction R5's flat connections modulo gauge type by type.

tests.name: torus
tests.statement: Torus G^ℝ: 𝒳 = Hom(Γ^{ab}, G^ℝ); U(1)^{2g} for π₁(Σ_g).

tests.name: non_hausdorff_naive
tests.statement: For Γ = ℤ, G^ℝ = SL₂(ℝ), the naive orbit space is not Hausdorff ([[1,1],[0,1]] and 1); 𝒳 is the semisimple classes.

tests.name: infinite_rank
tests.statement: Γ free of countably infinite rank, G^ℝ = ℝ^×: Ad trivial, every ρ reductive, conjugation trivial, 𝒳 = (ℝ^×)^ℕ, not locally compact; for rank m, (ℝ^×)^m is locally compact.

targets.name: CharacterVariety.affineQuotient
targets.statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, Hom(Γ,G)//G := Spec O(Hom(Γ,G))^G is a closed subscheme of G^S//G, of finite type, with the universal property; over an algebraically closed field points are closed orbits and points have the same image iff orbit closures meet. For k = ℂ, 𝒳(Γ,G(ℂ)) ≅ (Hom(Γ,G)//G)(ℂ) for the classical topology, and the quotient map is the universal Hausdorff quotient of Hom(Γ,G(ℂ))/G(ℂ).

tests.name: GLn_charpoly
tests.statement: Γ = ℤ, G = GL_n: Hom//G = 𝔸^{n−1} × 𝔾_m by the characteristic polynomial; 𝒳 = semisimple classes.

tests.name: free_SL2
tests.statement: Γ = F₂, G = SL₂: (Hom//G)(ℂ) ≅ ℂ³ via (tr a, tr b, tr ab).

tests.name: char_p
tests.statement: In characteristic p invariants of a closed invariant subscheme need not lift (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §1.11's C₂ example).

targets.name: CharacterVariety.map
targets.statement: Morphisms of real reductive data preserve reductivity and induce continuous maps on 𝒳; surjections Γ' ↠ Γ induce closed embeddings 𝒳(Γ) → 𝒳(Γ'); restriction to finite-index subgroups preserves reductivity and induces continuous maps.

tests.name: SO2_SL2
tests.statement: SO(2) ⊆ SL₂(ℝ) induces 𝒳(Γ,SO(2)) → 𝒳(Γ,SL₂(ℝ)).

tests.name: arbitrary_subgroup
tests.statement: Restriction from F₂ to ⟨a⟩ of a Zariski-dense ρ with ρ(a) unipotent is not reductive.

tests.name: quotient_Z2
tests.statement: 𝒳(ℤ/2,G^ℝ) is the closed subset of 𝒳(ℤ,G^ℝ) of classes of order dividing two.

targets.name: CharacterVariety.outAction
targets.statement: Out(Γ) acts on 𝒳(Γ,G^ℝ) by homeomorphisms, [φ]·[ρ] = [ρ ∘ φ⁻¹], restricting 1.3's action; for Γ = π₁(Σ_{g,n},x) basepoint paths give canonical homeomorphisms and Mod^±_{g,n} acts through Ψ_x compatibly with 3.5.

tests.name: GLr_semisimple
tests.statement: For GL_r(ℂ) the action is 3.5's action on semisimple classes; the unipotent example's orbit lies outside 𝒳.

tests.name: Z_inversion
tests.statement: Out(ℤ) acts on 𝒳(ℤ,SO(2)) = SO(2) by conjugation, fixing ±1.

tests.name: fuchsian
tests.statement: Fuch ⊆ 𝒳(π₁(Σ_g), PSL₂(ℝ)), Euler number 2 − 2g, is in Mod-equivariant bijection with Teich(Σ_g); reflection conjugates have Euler number 2g − 2.

targets.name: CharacterVariety.examples
targets.statement: Computed examples: Γ trivial gives a point; F_m with compact G^ℝ gives (G^ℝ)^m/G^ℝ; 𝒳(ℤ, GL₁(ℝ)) = ℝ^×; 𝒳(ℤ, PSL₂(ℝ)) is the elliptic and hyperbolic classes with the identity; 𝒳(π₁(Σ₁), GL₁(ℂ)) = (ℂ^×)²; 𝒳(π₁(Σ_{0,3}), SL₂(ℂ)) ≅ ℂ³.

tests.name: trivial_group
tests.statement: 𝒳(1, G^ℝ) is a point.

tests.name: PSL2_cyclic
tests.statement: Parabolic classes are absent from 𝒳(ℤ, PSL₂(ℝ)).

tests.name: pants_SL2C
tests.statement: 𝒳(π₁(Σ_{0,3}), SL₂(ℂ)) ≅ ℂ³.

The mapping class group Mod(F) of a compact smooth surface, its single owner; for closed F identified with MappingClassGroupFull F by TeichmullerGeometry §0.0h.

Affine group schemes, Lie algebras and Ad, closed orbits in orbit closures and boundary dimensions, unipotent radicals, characteristic-zero linear reductivity and the multiplicative centre, parabolics and cocharacters, split models.
The point topology on X(R) and Weil restriction.
The classical topology on complex points of finite-type complex schemes.

Scalar extension of semisimplicity over perfect fields; affine reductive quotients of integral affine varieties; G-complete reducibility, the GL(V) comparison, the closed-tuple criterion and the cocharacter limit into the closed orbit.
Real points as Lie groups, transpose-stable realizations, maximal compact subgroups and polar decomposition; algebraic Cartan involutions.

gaps.title: Completely reducible subgroups have reductive identity component
gaps.detail: For a connected reductive G over an algebraically closed field and a closed G-completely reducible subgroup H, H^0 is reductive (BateMartinRohrle2005 line 263, after Serre). Route: Borel-Tits places H in the parabolic P of R_u(H^0) with R_u(H^0) in R_u(P); a Levi subgroup of P containing H meets R_u(P) trivially.
gaps.needs: A proof that a G-completely reducible closed subgroup of a connected reductive group over an algebraically closed field has reductive identity component.

gaps.title: The Borel-Tits theorem
gaps.detail: For a closed unipotent subgroup U of a connected reductive group G over an algebraically closed field there is a parabolic P with U contained in R_u(P) and N_G(U) contained in P. Needed by the route of gcr-reductive-identity-component.
gaps.needs: The Borel-Tits theorem placing a closed unipotent subgroup and its normalizer in a parabolic whose unipotent radical contains it.
